title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2611.15216v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: \textbf{Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS)} aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prompt. translated_title: 我的杯子在哪里？一种免训练的个性化图像分割框架
translated_abstract: 个性化图像分割旨在从目标图像中分割出与用户提供的参考相匹配的特定对象。与基于类别的分割或小样本分割不同，个性化图像分割必须区分多个视觉上相似的实例，这一需求对于增强现实、个性化内容编辑、机器人操控、库存追踪以及细粒度视觉检索等实际部署的应用至关重要。我们表明，现有个性化图像分割方法所报告的优异结果在很大程度上是单实例基准测试造成的假象：当在包含多个同类相似物体的现实场景中进行评估时，先前基于点提示的方法会崩溃，因为正确的实例往往从未被作为提示呈现出来。我们将这一问题追溯为召回瓶颈而非掩码质量问题，并通过一个免训练的模块化系统加以解决。该流程首先使用现成的工具生成高召回率的物体候选建议……
tldr: 本文揭示现有个性化图像分割方法在包含多个相似实例的真实场景中会因提示召回瓶颈而失效，并提出了一种免训练的模块化框架来解决这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that existing personalized image segmentation methods collapse in realistic multi-instance scenes due to a prompt recall bottleneck, and proposes a training-free modular framework to address this issue.
